audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Luke prologue, Spirit promise, ascension, witness to ends of earth, upper room prayer, Judas/Scripture, Matthias.

verses.restored: The first account I made, O Theophilus, concerning all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,

familiar.text: The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach,

modern.text: In my first book, O Theophilus, I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,

original.text: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν

verses.restored: until the day when, having given commands through holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.

familiar.text: Until the day in which he was taken up, after that he through the Holy Ghost had given commandments unto the apostles whom he had chosen:

modern.text: until the day He was taken up to heaven, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles He had chosen.

original.text: ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·

verses.restored: To these he also presented himself alive after his suffering by many proofs, appearing to them through forty days and speaking the things concerning the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:

modern.text: After His suffering, He presented Himself to them with many convincing proofs that He was alive. He appeared to them over a span of forty days and spoke about the kingdom of God.

original.text: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, διʼ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ·

verses.restored: Gathered with them, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, which, he said, you heard from me.

familiar.text: And, being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye have heard of me.

modern.text: And while they were gathered together, He commanded them: “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised, which you have heard Me discuss.

original.text: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·

verses.restored: For John baptized in water, but you will be baptized in holy Spirit not many days from now.

familiar.text: For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.

modern.text: For John baptized with water, but in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit. ” The Ascension (Mark 16:19–20; Luke 24:50–53)

original.text: ὅτι Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ⸂ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε⸃ ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: Those therefore who had come together asked him, Lord, are you at this time restoring the reign to Israel?

familiar.text: When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?

modern.text: So when they came together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

original.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ⸀ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;

verses.restored: He said to them, It is not yours to know times or seasons that the Father set in his own authority.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ,

verses.restored: But you will receive power when the holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and as far as the end of the earth.

familiar.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

modern.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ ⸀μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρείᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: Saying these things, while they were beholding, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him from their eyes.

familiar.text: And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.

modern.text: After He had said this, they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.

original.text: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: As they were gazing into heaven while he was going, look, two men stood by them in white clothing,

familiar.text: And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel;

modern.text: They were looking intently into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.

original.text: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ⸂ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς⸃,

verses.restored: who also said, Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you beheld him going into heaven.

familiar.text: Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

modern.text: “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.” Matthias Replaces Judas

original.text: οἳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε ⸀βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφʼ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.

verses.restored: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away.

familiar.text: Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.

modern.text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is near the city, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

original.text: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἰερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.

verses.restored: When they entered, they went up into the upper room where they were remaining: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas of James.

familiar.text: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

modern.text: When they arrived, they went to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

original.text: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, ⸂εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν⸃ οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ ⸂Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἰάκωβος⸃ καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.

verses.restored: All these were persevering with one accord in prayer, together with women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.

familiar.text: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

modern.text: With one accord they all continued in prayer, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

original.text: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ ⸀προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ ⸀Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ⸀σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: In those days Peter stood up in the midst of the siblings, and the crowd of names was about one hundred twenty, and said,

familiar.text: And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, and said, (the number of names together were about an hundred and twenty,)

modern.text: In those days Peter stood up among the brothers (a gathering of about a hundred and twenty) and said,

original.text: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ⸀ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν (ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ⸀ὡς ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι)·

verses.restored: Men, siblings, it was necessary for the Scripture to be fulfilled, which the holy Spirit spoke beforehand through David's mouth concerning Judas, who became guide to those who seized Jesus.

familiar.text: Men and brethren, this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus.

modern.text: “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.

original.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν ⸀γραφὴν ἣν προεῖπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον διὰ στόματος Δαυὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τοῖς συλλαβοῦσιν ⸀Ἰησοῦν,

verses.restored: For he was numbered among us and received the allotment of this service.

familiar.text: For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.

modern.text: He was one of our number and shared in this ministry.”

original.text: ὅτι κατηριθμημένος ἦν ⸀ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης.—

verses.restored: This one therefore acquired a field from the wage of injustice; falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his inward parts poured out.

familiar.text: Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.

modern.text: (Now with the reward for his wickedness Judas bought a field; there he fell headlong and burst open in the middle, and all his intestines spilled out.

original.text: Οὗτος μὲν οὖν ἐκτήσατο χωρίον ἐκ μισθοῦ τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ πρηνὴς γενόμενος ἐλάκησεν μέσος, καὶ ἐξεχύθη πάντα τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: It became known to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.

familiar.text: And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.

modern.text: This became known to all who lived in Jerusalem, so they called that field in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)

original.text: καὶ γνωστὸν ἐγένετο πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ, ὥστε κληθῆναι τὸ χωρίον ἐκεῖνο τῇ ⸀ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ αὐτῶν Ἁκελδαμάχ, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χωρίον Αἵματος.—

verses.restored: For it has been written in the scroll of Psalms: Let his dwelling become deserted, and let there be no one dwelling in it; and, Let another take his overseer-service.

familiar.text: For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.

modern.text: “For it is written in the book of Psalms: ‘May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it,’ and, ‘May another take his position.’

original.text: γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· Γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος καὶ μὴ ἔστω ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, καί· Τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ ⸀λαβέτω ἕτερος.

verses.restored: Therefore it is necessary that of the men who accompanied us during all the time the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,

familiar.text: Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

modern.text: Therefore it is necessary to choose one of the men who have accompanied us the whole time the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

original.text: δεῖ οὖν τῶν συνελθόντων ἡμῖν ἀνδρῶν ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ ⸀ᾧ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς,

verses.restored: beginning from the baptism of John until the day he was taken up from us, one of these should become a witness with us of his resurrection.

familiar.text: Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.

modern.text: beginning from John’s baptism until the day Jesus was taken up from us. For one of these must become a witness with us of His resurrection.”

original.text: ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάννου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἀνελήμφθη ἀφʼ ἡμῶν, μάρτυρα τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ ⸂σὺν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι⸃ ἕνα τούτων.

verses.restored: They put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.

familiar.text: And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

modern.text: So they proposed two men: Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.

original.text: καὶ ἔστησαν δύο, Ἰωσὴφ τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν, ὃς ἐπεκλήθη Ἰοῦστος, καὶ Μαθθίαν.

verses.restored: Praying, they said, You, Lord, knower of all hearts, show which one of these two you have chosen

familiar.text: And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,

modern.text: And they prayed, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen

original.text: καὶ προσευξάμενοι εἶπαν Σὺ κύριε καρδιογνῶστα πάντων, ἀνάδειξον ὃν ἐξελέξω, ἐκ τούτων τῶν δύο ἕνα,

verses.restored: to take the place of this service and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place.

familiar.text: That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.

modern.text: to take up this ministry and apostleship, which Judas abandoned to go to his rightful place.”

original.text: λαβεῖν τὸν ⸀τόπον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης καὶ ἀποστολῆς, ⸀ἀφʼ ἧς παρέβη Ἰούδας πορευθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν ἴδιον.

verses.restored: They gave lots for them, and the lot fell to Matthias, and he was counted together with the eleven apostles.

familiar.text: And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

modern.text: Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.

original.text: καὶ ἔδωκαν κλήρους ⸀αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Μαθθίαν, καὶ συγκατεψηφίσθη μετὰ τῶν ἕνδεκα ἀποστόλων.
